newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: UN sees about 52.3M BBLS IRAQ OIL sold in 90 days.
newsitem.headline: UN sees about 52.3M BBLS IRAQ OIL sold in 90 days.

text.p: U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan said on Tuesday that Iraq had sold 52.3 million barrels worth $1.07 billion in the first three months under a U.N. oil-for-food deal.

The report, obtained by Reuters, and prepared shortly before the 90-day period ended on March 9, said that "43 loadings, totalling 44.7 million barrels, with an estimated value of $907.6 million" had been completed by then.
"If current market prices remain unchanged and the lifting programme is fulfilled," the report said, "total revenue generated should be within the range of the 90-day objective of $1.07 billion."

U.N. officials earlier confirmed that Iraq had hit its target of $1 billion in approved oil sales in the past three months, despite falling oil prices. But the report spelled out more clearly the quantity of the oil sold.

U.N. monitors or oil overseers in New York had reviewed a total of 38 contracts and approved 35 for the first three-month period, the report said. The sharp reduction in oil prices in February also resulted in spot contracts, it added.

"The overseers are confident that in the remainder of the 180-day period, Iraq would be able to export sufficient oil to generate" the $2 billion total allowed over six months under the terms of the deal, the report said.
The report also said that about 66 percent of the "liftings" had been made at the Ceyhan port in Turkey. The remainder presumably was shipped through Iraqi ports at Mina-al-Bakr.

The oil-for-food plan went into effect on December 10 and is to run for six months. Under the deal Iraq can sell $2 billion in oil to buy food and medicine for its people, suffering under sanctions since August 1990 when Baghdad's troops invaded Kuwait.
Oil proceeds are also used to pay compensation to victims of the Iraqi invasion and defray some U.N. costs.
